subject: Feature prioritization request — AtlasOne renewal dependency
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@atlasone.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Feature prioritization request — AtlasOne renewal dependency

Folks,

AtlasOne (renewal window: 2027-09-10) locked in a hard dependency during their legal/procurement review: they require a deterministic runtime snapshot export for audit + an explicit data-residency guarantee (us-west) for a renewal to be signed. They want the capability demonstrated in our environment before signatures.

I attached the draft SOW and a short renewal-summary PDF (see attachments). Ben/Monica are on the thread for context, but the ask is product + eng: can we commit to an MVP that provides a read-only runtime snapshot export (JSON-lines, token-level trace ids included) and routing pinning to a US-West region within ~3 weeks?

Key customer notes from Daniel: 
- They need an auditable export for compliance (SOC-type auditors)
- Export must include request metadata, model version, token-level ids, and timestamps
- Data must remain in US-West for the exported artifacts and for processing

Asks: 
1) Product: scope and acceptance criteria for a minimal ship that satisfies procurement/legal.
2) Eng: feasibility + rough ETA (number of sprints / engineering days).
3) Sales/CS: any flexibility on the format or acceptance bar we can negotiate.

This is high-impact: deal is currently at verbal agreement but procurement & legal paused. If we can get a concrete plan today, I will escalate to the customer and push the procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: AtlasOne_SOW_draft.docx, renewal-summary.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature prioritization request — AtlasOne renewal dependency

Thanks Vivek — adding a few clarifying questions so we scope RN-2247 correctly:

1) Desired SLA/Throughput: do they expect export to be triggered on every inference request (high QPS), or are they satisfied with scheduled snapshots (hourly/daily)? If the former, that changes the approach considerably.
2) Export format: you mentioned JSON-lines with token-level ids — is NDJSON acceptable? Any required schema we should match for their auditors?
3) Retention & retention authority: how long must we retain the exported snapshot and is AtlasOne requesting RW access to the export location?
4) Operational model: do they require a managed Pineapple-style dataset export in our console or an S3 bucket push they control?

We can create a narrow MVP: triggered snapshot endpoint that writes a signed, time-limited archive to a customer S3 bucket (read-only for them) and a routing flag to prefer US-West. That would cover audit exports without adding a continuous data path. But I need Eng input on the residency guarantee (pinning live requests vs routing preference).

I've opened RN-2247 in our backlog to track; I will add acceptance criteria once engineering confirms feasibility.

-Laura
Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.com>
To: laura.b@redwood.com
Cc: vivek.k@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature prioritization request — AtlasOne renewal dependency

Laura / team — quick feasibility notes from eng: 

- Snapshot/export: doable as an engineering task. We can add an on-demand snapshot endpoint that serializes the request/response traces, model version, and token-level metadata into NDJSON and export to S3. Estimated work: 1 sprint to implement (core plumbing + exporter), + half-sprint for security review & signed URL flow.

- Residency (routing pin): full hard pinning (guarantee that all inference for this customer will always run in US-West) requires changes in routing and capacity reservation and is more invasive — likely 2 sprints (routing flags, capacity affinity, testing).

- Quick compromise (MVP): provide the snapshot/export (1 sprint) and a sticky routing preference that biases to US-West but falls back if capacity is exhausted — this is lower risk and could be accepted by some customers if documented.

- Acceptance criteria we would need:
  * Snapshot endpoint returns an NDJSON archive containing per-request metadata, model hash, token-level trace ids, and timestamps
  * Export delivered to a pre-authorized S3 location with server-side encryption and signed URL for download
  * Routing preference flag applied at tenant metadata level + dashboard indicator

We can target the snapshot MVP to ship in the next sprint (starts Monday). If you need the routing hard-pin within 3 weeks, we will need to re-prioritize work from the roadmap — call that a deal-priority shift.

I'll add more technical notes in RN-2247; please confirm acceptance criteria and whether to escalate.

—Priyom
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>, laura.b@redwood.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, priyom.d@redwood.com, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@atlasone.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature prioritization request — AtlasOne renewal dependency

Quick update from AtlasOne (Dan just confirmed verbally and looped procurement):

- They are willing to accept a one-time demonstrable snapshot export delivered to their S3 as long as the exported artifact contains the requested token-level trace ids and model version.
- They still prefer a hard residency commit, but procurement sign-off can be satisfied with a documented routing preference plus an audit showing exports remained in US-West for the period in question.
- Customer timeline: they want the demonstrable export by 2027-09-03 so their auditors can validate prior to the renewal date. If we cannot show something by that date, they will pause the renewal and evaluate alternatives.

Attached: AtlasOne_SOW_draft.docx, renewal-summary.pdf (same as Vivek's). HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/ATLAS-4672

We need product/eng to confirm today whether the snapshot MVP (NDJSON to S3 + routing preference) is acceptable and whether RN-2247 can be bumped to deal-priority.

—Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
To: laura.b@redwood.com, priyom.d@redwood.com
Cc: ben.c@redwood.com, monica.p@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature prioritization request — AtlasOne renewal dependency

Laura / Priyom — following up and escalating: procurement made clear the export + residency demonstration is gating the close. Ben confirmed the programmatic acceptance criteria and the hard deadline (customer wants a demonstrable export by 2027-09-03).

Please mark RN-2247 as deal-priority and confirm one of the two paths by COB Monday (2027-08-23):
A) MVP commitment: snapshot NDJSON -> pre-authorized S3 with signed URL + routing preference (ETA: 1 sprint for snapshot, additional work to harden routing)
B) Hard-pin commitment: dedicate routing affinity / capacity changes (ETA: ~2 sprints; requires roadmap reprioritization)

Acceptance criteria to communicate to AtlasOne (please confirm these are feasible):
- Export format: NDJSON lines, including per-request metadata, model hash, token-level trace ids, timestamps
- Delivery: exported archive uploaded to customer's pre-authorized S3 with SSE and a signed URL for download (90-day availability)
- Residency: exported artifacts and processing must be restricted to us-west; if full hard-pin not possible, we can commit to routing preference plus audit logs showing processing locality for the export window

If product/eng can confirm path A by COB Monday, I will tell the customer we can meet their timeline and initiate procurement coordination. If not, I will escalate to my VP and ask for a cross-functional resourcing decision.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround on this one.

Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
